chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
"If one forgets to give the final salām (greeting of peace) behind the Imam, the Imam's salām suffices for him."

He said: I heard it being mentioned in the presence of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) that he said: "Regarding a man who makes a mistake in the Qunūt, he performs Qunūt after he has concluded (the prayer) while he is sitting."

key_terms.تَسْلِيمُ الْإِمَامِ: The Imam's final salām (greeting of peace)
key_terms.قَنَتَ: He performed the Qunūt (supplication in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person forgets to say the final greeting of peace behind the Imam or makes a mistake in the Qunūt?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of following the Imam during specific acts of worship, establishing that the Imam's final salām suffices for the follower who missed it, thereby emphasizing the validity of congregational unity. Additionally, it provides a practical remedy for errors in the Qunūt supplication, instructing the worshipper to repeat it after the prayer while seated, which reflects the Shia juristic preference for simplicity and ease in correcting ritual mistakes.
